Revisão 2026-07-28: o que mudou em uma t: Revision 2026-07-28: what changed on one screen
A versão vigente do protocolo é a <b>202: The current protocol version is 2026-07-28 (MCP versioning page, read on 10/19/2026). The previous one was 2025-11-25.
O que mais muda para quem vem de 2025: n: What changes the most for anyone coming from 2025: there is no more initialize handshake or session (Mcp-Session-Id); each request carries the version and capabilities in _meta; the client discovers the server with server/discover; and a server that needs to ask the user something returns input_required instead of opening its own request. Roots, Sampling, and Logging were deprecated.
O SDK oficial que implementa isso é a li: The official SDK that implements this is the v2 line (@modelcontextprotocol/server and @modelcontextprotocol/client, 2.3.1, from 10/05/2026). The old @modelcontextprotocol/sdk package (1.32.1) still speaks 2025-11-25: it's what you'll find in most tutorials.

Comece pela jornada da pessoa (\"achar u: Start from the person's journey ("find a class with a seat"), not from the name of a function in your code. Two tools that answer the same request make the model guess.
Curto e com verbo: <code>buscar_turmas</: Short and with a verb: buscar_turmas, reservar_vaga. The title is the label for people; the name is what the model calls.
Diz o que faz, quando usar e se tem cons: It says what the tool does, when to use it, and whether it has consequences. It's the only explanation the model gets, along with the description of each argument.
Zod vira JSON Schema 2020-12 no <code>to: Zod becomes JSON Schema 2020-12 in tools/list. The SDK validates before the handler: an argument outside the schema comes back as isError and your code doesn't even run.
<code>readOnlyHint</code>, <code>destruc: readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint. The client uses them to decide whether to approve on its own or ask. They are hints: they don't change execution, and a client shouldn't trust them when they come from an unknown server.
<code>content</code> para o modelo ler e: content for the model to read and, with outputSchema, structuredContent validated by the SDK before it goes out.
Semântica das anotações conforme o tipo: Annotation semantics per the ToolAnnotations type in the 2026-07-28 revision (official SDK code, 10/13/2026).
Os padrões da especificação valem quando: The specification's defaults apply when you omit the annotation.
true = the tool doesn't change the environment. A host can approve a read-only tool on its own.
Sem a anotação, o cliente deve supor que: Without the annotation, the client should assume it changes something.
Only makes sense when the tool is not read-only. true = can delete or overwrite; false = only adds (like a new booking).
Omitir numa ferramenta que muda algo = o: If you leave it out on a tool that changes something, the client treats it as destructive.
true = repetir com os mesmos argumentos: true = repeating the call with the same arguments has no extra effect. It matters because clients retry calls (the network dropped, MRTR in lesson 5).
<code>reservar_vaga</code> não é idempot: reservar_vaga is not idempotent: two calls, two seats.
true = fala com o mundo externo (busca n: true = talks to the outside world (web search, third-party API). false = closed domain, like the kit's in-memory catalog.
Ferramenta de mundo aberto é porta de en: An open-world tool is an entry point for untrusted content: course 4 covers this.

Idempotent means repeating has no extra effect. Two identical bookings take two seats, so the client should not blindly retry.

Corpo JSON-RPC com <code>_meta</code>: v: JSON-RPC body with _meta: protocol version, client name and capabilities. It goes in every request, because there is no session to remember.
<code>MCP-Protocol-Version</code>, <code: MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and, on methods with a name (like tools/call), Mcp-Name. A load balancer or firewall can route without opening the JSON. The server checks that they match the body.
Antes do handler: no localhost, a checag: Before the handler: on localhost, the Host check blocks DNS rebinding (a malicious page pointing its own domain to 127.0.0.1). The SDK handler does not do this by itself.
<code>createMcpHandler(createServer)</co: createMcpHandler(createServer) builds a new McpServer on every request. The protocol keeps nothing between requests; your service's data (database, cache) lives outside the factory.
